title: The King's word and the deed: Malchus of Malchus
overview:
The chapter's first part, on the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, their *katnus* and *gadlus*, and their vessels, the letters of thought, speech and action within speech, has no recording in this series. The class picks up at action within speech. Speech itself is a deed, the moving of the lips, even when it tells nobody to do anything: "And G-d said, Let there be light" is action in speech.

Then comes the deed that comes out of the word. King Achashverosh did not mop the floor; he said "Make a party," and there was a party, because he was the king. The word is *Malchus*; the party, "and there was light", is *Malchus* of *Malchus*. And there is a *Malchus* of *Malchus* still in *Atzilus*, before the screen: the minute the king passes a law or the judge decrees, the deed has begun, though no street sign has changed and no lash has fallen. So the ten utterances are said in *Atzilus*, and they are being said right now. If "Let there be light" stopped, the fabric of the universe would disappear.

terms.gloss: action, a deed; even speech that commands nothing is one, the moving of the lips
a decree of the king, from which the actual deed comes out
the Malchus of Malchus: the deed that comes out of the King's word, "and there was light"; already there in Atzilus while He is saying it, before it breaks through the screen
the screen between Atzilus and Beriya, which the Malchus of Malchus breaks through
the breaking through the screen; there is a Malchus of Malchus before it and one after it, like a new law before the street signs are changed
the power of the act, which separates from the maker and goes into the thing made
the power of the maker; it is also action, and stays with the king: that is Malchus
the thing made, into which something goes out of the maker's power
the act, the happening; it begins the minute the king or the judge says it
the thickening of the light; all the stuff in front of you, atoms and strings, comes from it
the ten utterances of creation, said in Atzilus and being said right now

sections.title: The ten sefiros of Malchus of Atzilus: its Keser, its wisdom and its middos (not on tape)
sections.summary: *Malchus* of *Atzilus* has ten *sefiros* (Divine attributes) of its own: its *Keser* is the simple delight and will revealed in this attribute; the will contracts into *chachma* and *bina*, the lower wisdom rooted in the higher; then come its *middos*, as "a king establishes the land with justice", and through them the work of creation is renewed every day. The series has no recording of these lines.

skip.note: Class 228, the only class on this chapter, begins at line 32; the class that taught lines 1-31 is not in the catalog.

sections.title: Katnus and gadlus in the sefiros of Malchus (not on tape)
sections.summary: Like those of *Zeir Anpin*, the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus* are sometimes in *katnus* (smallness) and sometimes in *gadlus* (greatness): at times the mind spreads broadly into the *middos* revealed in speech, at times the *middos* are as small as a point, as with the difference between weekdays, *Shabbos* and Yom Kippur. The series has no recording of these lines.

sections.title: The vessels of Malchus are the letters of speech: thought within speech and speech within speech (not on tape)
sections.summary: The vessels of the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* are the letters of the speech of the ten utterances, in three levels. Thought within speech, the vessel of its *Chabad*, is the particular thought dressed in each particular word, as the thought of "Let there be light" in that utterance; speech within speech, the vessels of *Chagas*, is the letters of the king's word of kindness or judgement itself. The series has no recording of these lines.

sections.title: Action within speech: the command to act, and speech itself as a deed
sections.summary: The vessels of *Nehi* of *Malchus* are speech that commands an actual deed, as a king first decrees and then orders it done (not on tape). And speech itself is a deed, the moving of the lips, even where the words tell nobody to do anything: "And G-d said, Let there be light" is action in speech.

phrases.en: The *dibur* itself is a *maaseh*: not that the *dibur* is commanding a *maaseh*, but the *dibur* itself is a *maaseh* that he does with his mouth.

phrases.he: שנקרא עשיה שבדבור גם כן, הענין הוא מה שנחתך הדבור לבוא לידי פועל ממש שהפה גומר, לפי שיש דבור שאינו למעשה עדיין כו')
וזה שכתוב ויאמר אלהי״ם יהי אור ורקיע, במעשה דוקא
phrases.en: He said there should be light in actuality.

blocks.text: Speech itself is a *maaseh* (an action). Not speech that commands an action: the *dibur* (speech) itself is a deed, one a person does with his mouth, and so it is called action in speech too.

Rabbi Markel does not know exactly what is meant here. He thinks there can be speech with no *inyan* (matter) of action in it, telling nobody to do anything, like the question "*Vos tut zich in Atzilus?*", what is going on in *Atzilus*? That is not really an action, so there the action is moving the lips. That is "And *Elokim* said, Let there be light": action in speech *davka* (specifically). **He said there should be light in actuality.**

sections.title: The deed that comes out of the King's word: Malchus of Malchus
sections.summary: Achashverosh said "Make a party" and there was a party; the *Aibershter* said "Let there be light" and there was light. The word that says what to do is *Malchus*; the deed that comes out of it, which breaks through the screen to be the source of creation, is *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

phrases.en: And then there's the actual *maaseh* that came out of his *dibur*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב ויהי אור וכהאי גוונא,
כדבר מלך שנעשה מזה הפועל ממש,
phrases.en: The actual *poel* that came out of the *gezeira* of the king.

The actual thing that came out of it, not the thing that he spoke and said what to do, *yehi or*: that's *Malchus*. But actually *vayehi or*, and there was a light: that's called *Malchus sheb'Malchus*.

phrases.he: שאין זה רק בבוא שפע אור בבחינת מקור התהוות יש מאין ממש כו',
phrases.en: That's only when it comes out in a way of bringing an actual something out of nothing.

phrases.he: והיינו בחינת מלכות דמלכות דאצילות שבוקע המסך להיות מקור לבריאה

blocks.title: Achashverosh's party
blocks.text: Then there is **the actual *maaseh* that came out of his *dibur***, like "and there was light": the deed that comes out of the king's *gezeira* (decree). King Achashverosh said, "We're going to make a party," and there was a party. The *Megilla* says King Achashverosh made a party, but he made nothing. He did not clean the whole place with a mop and get all the food and drinks ready; he sat on his throne and said, "Make a party." So where was his deed? He said it, and from that came the actual deed: there really was a party, and some party, one nobody else could have made however hard he worked. Because he was the king, saying "I want a party" was enough.

So with the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d). "Let there be light", the word saying what to do, is *Malchus*; "and there was light", the party that was made, is *Malchus d'Malchus*, the *Malchus* of *Malchus*. That is **only when it comes out in a way of bringing an actual something out of nothing**: the *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* that breaks through the *masach* (the screen) to be the source of *Beriya*.

sections.title: Malchus of Malchus is still in Atzilus: the word is already the deed
sections.summary: There is a *Malchus* of *Malchus* before the screen: the power in the king's word that goes out into the thing made, so that the deed begins the minute he speaks, like a king's new law or a judge's sentence. So the ten utterances are said in *Atzilus*, and are being said right now: if they stopped, the world would disappear.

phrases.en: This also is really still in *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: על דרך משל כח הפעולה הנבדלת מכח הפועל,
דגם שכח הפועל בחינת כח המעשה הוא,
אבל מה שיוצא מכחו בנפעל בחינת מלכות דמלכות הוא,
phrases.en: There's a thing that goes out of it into the *nifal*.

blocks.text: **This also is really still in *Atzilus***. *Malchus* of *Malchus* does not mean after it went through the screen: there is a *Malchus* of *Malchus* before the screen, which will be *boke'a* (break through) the screen. Then the line's example is read: the power of the act, separate from the power of the maker.

blocks.question: Malchus of Malchus was that the party was actually made, or that there was a light or a firmament. How is it Malchus of Malchus if it is still before it breaks through the screen into Beriya?
blocks.text: He answers: it is still part of the speech of the king himself, before it breaks through the screen. There is a *Malchus* of *Malchus* before the *bki'as hamasach* (the breaking through the screen) and a *Malchus* of *Malchus* after it.

The *Malchus* of *Malchus* before the screen is the power of the thing that will go into the *nifal* (the thing made): the power in Achashverosh's speech to make a party like that. It was there in his speech because he was the king.

blocks.title: A party in Pittsburgh
blocks.text: If a person says, "Hey, let's make a party, and I want the whole world to come. Everybody come to Pittsburgh, I expect everybody at my party," it doesn't mean nothing. There is no *Malchus* of *Malchus* in it, because there is no power to do it. There are certain things he does have the power to do.

So in "Let there be light, and there was light", the light is already there before the actual light. The minute Achashverosh said to make a party, that was the beginning of the actual party, because he gave the command.

blocks.title: The king's law: drive on the left
blocks.text: Say a king, instead of Congress, passes a law that from now on everybody drives on the left side of the street. The *bki'as hamasach* is everybody running around the whole country changing all the street signs. But the minute he said the law, that was already the *Malchus* of *Malchus*: still part of the *Malchus* itself, before it separates out to go and do what the king said.

So with the *Aibershter*: the minute He says "Let there be light", even before the *bki'as hamasach*. And remember, this is happening right now. If the utterance "Let there be light" stopped, the fabric of the universe would disappear, as the scientists say that matter is made out of energy. That is why the first thing He had to say was "Let there be light."

His saying "Let there be light" is what makes this light that is *metzamtzem* (contracted) through *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* until it makes the vessels of our world, the *hisabus or* (the thickening of the light): all the stuff in front of you comes from it. Atoms, electrons, protons, and now strings, are basically concentrations of lights within vessels. And what are the vessels made of? Energy too, they say. So the whole thing depends on the utterance "Let there be light", that there be this energy to fuel it all.
This really happens before *Beriya*, in *Atzilus*. The ten *maamaros* (utterances) happen in *Atzilus*: the King Himself says them, and the fact that He says them makes them happen.

His power is not like Achashverosh's. Look at Saddam: now he can say whatever he wants and nobody listens to him, because his power really came from their being scared of him. Or Bush: his comes from their having accepted him, voted for him.

sensitivity.reason: Names living political leaders (Saddam Hussein, out of power at the time, and President Bush) as examples of a ruler's borrowed power; the line on Saddam is a jab at a named person.

blocks.text: The *Aibershter* comes from Himself, so His power comes from Himself too. The very fact that He said it is what brings it into being. And it is not that He said it once, before.

That is what the Baal Shem Tov said on "Forever, G-d, Your word stands in the heavens." If the *Aibershter* stopped saying the utterance "Let there be light" and the rest of the ten utterances, if He stopped saying that there should be plants, all the plants would disappear. If He stopped saying that the waters should go off the earth and the land come up, it would go back to being an *igul* (a circle) inside an *igul*.

The *igul* of the earth was inside the *igul* of the water, until the *Aibershter* said to take the water off the earth and show dry land, the same as the *igul* of the air surrounds us. So when we speak of before and after with these utterances, as if He said it and now it is like this, it is not a before and after in time. It is happening *mamash* (literally) right now.

Back to the line: the *koach hapeula* (the power of the act) is separate from the *koach hapoel* (the power of the maker). The power of the maker is also action, and that is really *Malchus*. What goes out of it into the *nifal* is *Malchus* of *Malchus*: since an actual body came into being, at some point the power had to separate out into the act itself.

That is the difference between *Malchus* and *Malchus* of *Malchus*. The power of *Malchus* does not go through the screen; it stays with the king: that he said it, and that he is the king with the power of a king. But something went out from him, and it separated into *Malchus* of *Malchus* while it was still inside *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, while he was saying it.

blocks.title: The judge's sentence
blocks.text: His saying it already made it the beginning of the happening, the *peula* (the act). Like a judge: the minute he decrees, that is the beginning of the sentence. Later they will lock the man up; he is not locked up yet, they have not given him forty lashes, but he is already crying. What are you crying about, nothing happened? The judge said it already, and that means it did happen: it is already in the way of a *peula*. That is *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

reviewQuestions.question: How is speech itself an action, even when it tells nobody to do anything?
How did King Achashverosh make a party, and what does it show about Malchus and Malchus of Malchus?
How can there be a Malchus of Malchus before the screen, still in Atzilus?
What would happen if the utterance "Let there be light" stopped, and why?
Why is a man already crying when the judge decrees, though nothing has happened to him yet?

notes.text: Lines 1-31 have no recording. Class 227 (chapter 48) ends inside chapter 48, and class 228 opens in the middle of a sentence on line 32 ("Then is the fact that the dibur itself is a maaseh"); the class that taught lines 1-31 (and any end of chapter 48) is not in the catalog. The titles and summaries of sections 1-3 and the first part of section 4's summary paraphrase the chapter text, not a class.

Line 32: he says "I don't know exactly what he means by this" and gives his reading with "I think"; the block keeps his hesitation. The English of the line's first phrase (w7-45) is said before the transcript's reading of the rest of the line (w46-68); the rest of the line has no English.
Line 34: the English of "הוא ענין מלכות דמלכות דאצילות" is his explanation after the Achashverosh mashal (w514-562), where he calls it "Malchus sheb'Malchus"; the phrase keeps his words.
Line 35: he reads "כמו שיתבאר במקום אחר" where the text has "כמו שיתבאר ודי למבין"; his "and this'll be explained later" is given to the last phrase.

Line 37 is read at w671-698 without translation; the English of its second and third phrases is from his reread at w1834-1881. "It's also maaseh" is all he says for "דגם שכח הפועל בחינת כח המעשה הוא".

w1237-1241 ("It's not the same thing.") is unclear in context and is left out of the keyPoint block. w1721-1736 ("Yeah, that the igul of the earth...") may be a listener's answer to his "You know what I'm talking about?"; the block writes it as his explanation.
The aside on Saddam and Bush dates the class to about 2003-2004 ("now Saddam could say whatever he wants, nobody's listening to him").
From w2261 the tape goes on to chapter 50.
